column1: # AIOS scopes (a.k.a. "layers") — how this vault partitions knowledge.
# A scope is a bucket of context: a job, a side project, a client, a life area.
# Its purpose is ROUTING. It keeps one project's accumulated memory from bleeding
# into an unrelated one, and tells the AI which "me" file to read for a task.
# ONE SCOPE IS A COMPLETELY NORMAL SETUP. The default below is exactly that.
# Add rows only when you actually have contexts that shouldn't share memory.
# Tab-separated. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# Columns:
#   1. layer          Short slug. Must match AIOS/me-<layer>.md and Sources/<layer>/.
#   2. label          Human-readable name, used in messages.
#   3. content-globs  Pipe-separated shell globs of folders holding this scope's
#                     content. Scaffolding (AIOS/, Calendar/, x/) is excluded by
#                     design — it describes every scope.
#   4. tokens         OPTIONAL. "-" disables the wall for this scope (the default).
#                     See "Strict separation" below before filling this in.
#   5. allow-from     OPTIONAL. Pipe-separated scopes tolerated inside this one.
#                     "-" means strict. Only meaningful when tokens are set.
# DEFAULT: one scope, no wall. Most people want this.
# layer
main
# MULTIPLE SCOPES (still no wall) — routing only. Common and useful:
# work project memory stays out of personal project memory.
# work
# personal
# STRICT SEPARATION (the wall) — OPT-IN. You probably do not need this.
# Turn it on only if two scopes must never appear in the same file, and a
# mistake would be materially harmful rather than merely untidy. Real cases:
#   - A pen name or stage name that must never be linked to a legal name.
#   - Employer-proprietary work that must never reach a public portfolio,
#     a résumé, a blog post, or a job application.
#   - Client A's internals that must never surface in Client B's repo.
# To enable, fill column 4 with a case-insensitive regex of the strings that
# IDENTIFY that scope — names, brands, domains, codenames. The write-time guard
# (.claude/hooks/vault-write-guard.sh) then blocks any scope's tokens from
# landing in another scope's content folders, and the `layer-leak-auditor`
# subagent catches the inferred crossings a grep cannot.
# The wall is symmetric by default. Column 5 makes it one-way: `work` below
# tolerates `professional` (same legal person) but `professional` still refuses
# every `work` token, so employer detail can never reach the public brand.
# professional
# pen
# work
# Leaving column 4 as "-" keeps the guard inert for that scope. Nothing else
# in the vault changes. Turn it on later by editing this one file.
